entities.name: Farrukhzad Khosrau V
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Farrukhzad Khosrau V was the brief king of the Sasanian Empire from March 631 to April 631. He succeeded his father, Khosrau II, and ruled for only a few months before being deposed. During his short reign, Farrukhzad implemented various economic reforms aimed at revitalizing the empire's struggling economy.

Farrukhzad's reign was marked by power struggles between him and his brothers, who eventually conspired against him. His death in April 631 led to a period of instability in the empire, paving the way for the rise of the Rashidun Caliphate.

Despite his brief tenure, Farrukhzad Khosrau V played a significant role in shaping the course of Sasanian history. His policies and actions had lasting consequences for the empire's economy and politics, cementing his place as one of the most important figures in the empire's history.
